messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High 502/504 spike observed at gateway-edge cluster. Error rate > 8% p95 across apigw-frontend. Initial alert threshold breached. Allocated priority: P1.
Ashley: seeing it on the dashboard too. 502s across multiple regions, Europe first, now US-east. Any recent deploys?
Devon: no deploys from infra this morning — I just checked deploybot. Could be upstream timeouts or proxy overload.
Maria: customer reports starting to come in via support channel. A few timeouts, some 502s for file uploads.
Jonathan: grabbing logs and traces. Kicking off a quick query on request latencies: `kql: service:apigw* | where code in (502,504) | stats count(), p95(latency)`
infra-oncall: I’m scaling the gateway pool by +2 nodes in us-east-1 as a temporary mitigation. Starting now.
Ashley: good. Can someone confirm whether this coincides with any spike in large request sizes or unknown backend?
Devon: checking upstream health: proxy->model-router shows increased 504s on two hosts: mr-03 and mr-07. mr-07 CPU is spiking.
Maria: support note: customers seeing intermittent failures, some retries succeed. Severity message to customers draft: "We're investigating elevated gateway errors; traffic may see intermittent 502/504s. We're working on remediation."
incident-bot: (automated) Linked runbook: /runbooks/gateway-502-spike. Suggested mitigations: toggle fallback, throttle large uploads, scale pool, enable canary fallback model.
Jonathan: running tail on envoy logs for affected nodes: ```bash
kubectl -n gateway logs -l app=envoy -c envoy --tail=200 | grep "upstream reset" -i
```
Devon: found repeated `upstream connect error or disconnect` entries pointing to model-router TCP resets. Possibly hitting connection limits.
Ashley: let's try short-term: (1) enable connection pooling throttle, (2) add retry with jitter, (3) shift a percentage of traffic to secondary region to reduce pressure. I can open an emergency policy change.
infra-oncall: implemented a traffic shift of 20% to eu-west-1 to relieve us-east. Applied via traffic-router. Confirming metrics now.
Maria: added support message to status page draft and notified CS to escalate enterprise customers.
Devon: also temp disabled large file uploads by returning 413 for payloads > 50MB at the edge while we stabilize. Patch applied to edge-config.
Jonathan: checking if any recent config pushed to envoy — no config pushes in last 45m. So likely downstream service flapping.
Ashley: ok we need to isolate: can we isolate model-router mr-07 and restart? If it's unhealthy, drain and restart.
Devon: draining mr-07 now: `kubectl drain mr-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Restarting pods.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling restart of model-router/mr-07 started by Devon. (ETA ~90s per pod)
Maria: customer impact: ~12 support tickets flagged as high, 3 enterprise customers on the phone. I will patch the status page with the mitigation steps and update every 15m.
Jonathan: after restart, upstream resets dropped by ~70%. 502 rate fell to ~3.4% from 8.7% in the last 10 minutes. Latency p95 also down 120ms.
Ashley: nice. Keep scaling until stable. Also add a temporary ingress-level rate limit for suspicious client IPs causing huge concurrency.
Devon: added a quick ACL to block a small set of IPs that were hammering long-lived uploads. Bumped retry budget on envoy to 2.
infra-oncall: monitoring retention: if 502 < 1% for 15m, we consider reducing traffic shift and re-enabling uploads.
Maria: support update posted. Customers asked for ETA; I told them we'll have a clearer update in 15 minutes.
Jonathan: looking at traces, root cause looks like a combination: (1) a noisy client creating many concurrent connections for large uploads, (2) model-router instances hitting file-descriptor/thread limits, (3) transient congestion at the edge.
Ashley: longer-term: open infra ticket to increase FD limits and harden connection queue handling on model-router. Also add a circuit-breaker per upstream to fail-fast when OS limits reached.
Devon: will follow up in infra backlog. For now, 502 rate steady at ~1.2% after restarts and shifts. Still a few 504s but dropping.
incident-bot: (automated) Incident P1 active. Incident timeline logging started. Use `/incident update` to add notes.
Maria: I'm preparing a post-incident summary template; collecting timeline and customer impact numbers. Will include number of affected requests, timeframe, and mitigation actions.
Ashley: handing off monitoring and next steps to Devon and infra-oncall for the next 30 minutes while I go brief leadership. Tagging Devon as primary.
Devon: ack — I'll keep watch, will revert traffic shift incrementally when 502 < 0.5% for 10m. Noted to reopen if error rate climbs.
pagerduty-bot: Acknowledgement recorded for on-call: Devon. Next handoff scheduled at +30m.
Maria: final note for thread: collecting SLO hit numbers for the last hour and saving logs to the incident bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1769801200/`
Ashley: thanks everyone. Please keep the thread updated with any customer escalation. I'll join back for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
Devon: will continue monitoring. Closing active mitigations when stable and will annotate the timeline.
pagerduty-bot: Incident P1 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
Maria: adding this to the incident tracker and assigning postmortem owners: Ashley (lead), Devon (infra), Jonathan (logs/traces).
Ashley: good work.
